metadata.title: Why the Tumor That Shrank in Mice Won't Shrink in Patients
metadata.purpose: vox-explainer slate cut of Cancer Nanomedicine card 18. Source chapter: cancer-nanomedicine/chapters/12-clinical-strategy-and-the-gap-book.md. Mechanism: subcutaneous mouse xenograft is an EPR-maximum system; human solid tumors run EPR at variable-and-often-low.
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL #1F6F5C = mouse xenograft / open EPR / good accumulation; CRIMSON #BF3339 = human desmoplastic tumor / blocked EPR / low accumulation. Never swapped mid-film.
metadata.note: Card exclusions honored: NO BIND-014 trial specifics, NO IFP derivation, NO stromal enzyme or mechanical disruption strategies, NO active vs passive targeting debate. One mechanism only: the mouse model runs EPR at max; patients run EPR at variable-and-often-low.

beats.narration_text: A targeted nanoparticle fills mouse tumors with drug. In patients with the same cancer, the particles pile up in the liver instead.

items.label: In mice
items.sub: A targeted nanoparticle fills the tumor with drug

items.label: In patients
items.sub: Same cancer — the particles pile up in the liver

items.label: Same chemistry
items.sub: No change in the molecule explains the swap

beats.new_visual_element: [TITLE] mouse vs patient — the swap the mechanism must explain

beats.narration_text: A docetaxel nanoparticle accumulates in a subcutaneous mouse tumor. Mice respond. Preclinical accumulation reaches 8 percent of injected dose per gram. The data signals a breakthrough.

items.label: Docetaxel NP
items.sub: Accumulates in a subcutaneous mouse tumor

items.label: Mice respond
items.sub: Tumors shrink in the animal model

items.label: ~8% ID/g
items.sub: Preclinical accumulation reads as breakthrough

beats.narration_text: The same particle enters a phase two clinical trial. Tumor accumulation across the patient population drops and scatters widely. Many lesions see near-zero delivery. The chemistry did not change.

props.title: Phase II — the same particle in patients

items.label: Drops and scatters
items.sub: Accumulation collapses across the patient population

items.label: Near-zero lesions
items.sub: Many tumors see almost none of the dose

items.label: Chemistry unchanged
items.sub: The molecule is identical — the world is not

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] the drop from mouse to patient — same molecule

beats.narration_text: A cancer nanoparticle reliably delivered drug to tumors in mice. In patients with the same tumor type, it mostly ended up in the liver. The molecule was identical. Why?

items.label: In mice
items.sub: Reliable drug delivery to the tumor

items.label: In patients
items.sub: Same tumor type — particles end up in the liver

items.label: Same molecule
items.sub: The chemistry is identical — so why the swap?

beats.narration_text: Tumor vasculature is leaky — fenestrations wide enough to pass nanoparticles. Lymphatics are defective, so particles that enter do not drain away. Together, these produce passive accumulation in tumors without any active targeting. This is EPR.

items.label: Leaky vessels
items.sub: Fenestrations wide enough for nanoparticles to cross

items.label: Broken drainage
items.sub: Defective lymphatics — nothing flushes what enters

items.label: Passive uptake
items.sub: No active targeting required to pile up

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] EPR schematic — leaky vessel, no drainage

beats.narration_text: EPR is real and functions in the laboratory. Subcutaneous mouse xenografts — cancer cell lines in immunocompromised mice, grown under the skin — have thin-walled, maximally leaky vessels and no dense stroma. The model runs EPR at its upper limit.

props.title: Where EPR is maximum — the xenograft

items.label: The model
items.sub: Subcutaneous xenograft from cancer cell lines

items.label: Thin walls
items.sub: Maximally leaky vessels under the skin

items.label: No stroma
items.sub: Tumor grows in soft tissue — EPR at its upper limit

beats.narration_text: Human solid tumors differ structurally. Pancreatic and prostate cancers grow a dense fibrous scaffold — desmoplastic stroma. It compresses microvessels. It closes fenestrations. EPR stops functioning.

items.label: Desmoplastic stroma
items.sub: Dense fibrous scaffold in pancreatic, prostate, others

items.label: Compressed vessels
items.sub: Microvessels squeezed by fibers — lumens shrink

items.label: Closed gaps
items.sub: Fenestrations close — EPR stops functioning

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] fibrous strands compress vessel — EPR blocked

beats.narration_text: Human tumors also generate high interstitial fluid pressure — a sustained outward flow from inside the lesion that physically displaces particles before they accumulate. This force has no equivalent in the xenograft model.

props.title: High interstitial pressure — the outward push

items.label: Sustained flow
items.sub: High IFP builds inside the lesion

items.label: Outward direction
items.sub: Displaces particles before they can accumulate

items.label: No mouse analog
items.sub: This force has no equivalent in the xenograft

beats.narration_text: The mouse model tests nanoparticle delivery under maximum EPR conditions. Patients present EPR at its real-world average — highly variable between lesions and between patients, and often far lower than the preclinical model implies.

items.label: Mouse model
items.sub: EPR at maximum — the top of the range

items.label: Patient average
items.sub: Variable between lesions, often far lower

items.label: The gap
items.sub: Between the preclinical ideal and the human real

beats.narration_text: This is not a failure of the EPR mechanism. It is a failure of experimental logic. A nanoparticle optimized in a maximum-EPR system has not been tested under the conditions it will face in patients. The model does not represent the target population.

props.title: Not the mechanism — the experimental logic

items.label: EPR is real
items.sub: The mechanism is not what failed

items.label: Logic failed
items.sub: Optimized in max-EPR, never stressed under low-EPR

items.label: Wrong population
items.sub: Model does not represent the human target

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] EPR spectrum — mouse at max, patient scatter

beats.narration_text: Particles that miss their tumor target default to the liver and spleen, cleared by macrophages that patrol those organs. The patient's healthy tissue receives the dose the tumor was supposed to receive.

items.label: Liver default
items.sub: Macrophages sweep circulating particles

items.label: Spleen too
items.sub: Same reticuloendothelial trap catches the rest

items.label: Healthy tissue dosed
items.sub: The tumor's dose lands in the wrong organ

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] body silhouette — particles flood liver, trickle to tumor

beats.narration_text: Two tumor cross-sections, side by side. The xenograft: vessel fenestrations 200 nanometers wide, nanoparticles stream through, accumulation at 8 percent of injected dose per gram of tissue. These are illustrative numbers.

items.label: Fenestrations
items.sub: ~200 nm — open channels in the vessel wall

items.label: Accumulation
items.sub: ~8% ID/g — particles stream in freely

items.label: The system
items.sub: EPR at maximum, no mechanical barriers

beats.narration_text: The human desmoplastic tumor: stromal fibers compress vessels to near-closure. Accumulation drops to 0.3 percent of injected dose per gram. Same chemistry. Same diagnosis. The difference is structural — researchers term it interpatient EPR variability. Numbers are illustrative.

items.label: Vessels
items.sub: Compressed to near-closure by stromal fibers

items.label: Accumulation
items.sub: ~0.3% ID/g — same chemistry, ~8x less delivery

items.label: The label
items.sub: Researchers call it interpatient EPR variability

beats.narration_text: The nanoparticle did not fail. The model did. The subcutaneous xenograft is EPR at maximum: thin walls, no stroma, no outward pressure. The patient tumor is EPR at its real average: compressed, fibrous, resistant. Same molecule. Structurally different target.

items.label: Xenograft
items.sub: Thin walls, no stroma, no interstitial pressure

items.label: Patient tumor
items.sub: Compressed, fibrous, pushing particles back

items.label: The lesson
items.sub: The experimental model failed — not the drug
